summary.tagline: Ascend the highest mountain in southern Britain for expansive views across the Beacons.
summary.seo_title: Hiking Pen y Fan: Peak Routes and Safety Guide

travel.headline: Monitor Pont ar Daf Capacity and Summit Conditions
travel.reservation: No entry permit is required for the mountain, but parking at Pont ar Daf is limited and fills quickly during peak periods. The National Trust requests that visitors have a backup plan or return another time if designated spaces are full. Always check in with the Welcome Team at the car park to verify current summit conditions before starting your ascent.

days.title: Summit of the Southern Beacons
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Pont ar Daf car park

stops.name: Pen y Fan
stops.detail: Hike to the 886-metre summit to see the skyline shared with Corn Du and Cribyn peaks. Expect a steep climb involving rough terrain and fast-changing mountain weather.

days.driving: Allow for local transit to the trailheads; travel times vary based on regional traffic.
days.note: Pace your ascent according to group capability and be prepared for weather that is significantly colder and windier at the summit than at the base.

intel.title: Pont ar Daf Capacity
intel.text: This is the most popular starting point, and visitors should avoid irresponsible parking if the lot is full. Have a secondary destination in mind as parking is restricted to designated spaces only.

intel.title: Welcome Team Check-in
intel.text: Consult the National Trust Welcome Team at the car park before setting off. They provide real-time updates on summit safety and can answer specific route questions.

intel.title: Seasonal Weather Shifts
intel.text: The Beacons present challenges in any season, requiring waterproofs and insulating layers even in summer. Ensure you have a map and compass accessible, as visibility can drop rapidly.

intel.title: Emergency Communication
intel.text: Carry a fully charged phone and a whistle to signal for rescue if needed. The standard signal is six long blasts followed by a one-minute pause.

intel.title: Regional Supplies
intel.text: Evidence does not specify fuel or supply locations near the trailhead; confirm your resources in nearby towns before arrival. Always carry more water than you expect to need for the steep terrain.

plan.arrival: Arrive early at the Pont ar Daf car park to secure a space and meet with the Welcome Team for a safety briefing. Ensure your group is equipped with sturdy walking boots and appropriate layers for the 886-metre ascent.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for reaching the main car park, but check local road conditions during winter months.
plan.goldenHour: The summit provides expansive views of Corn Du, though sunset hikers must carry a torch with spare batteries as daylight fades quickly on the descent.
